ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r11.claim: Husr means losing rather than gaining, wasting capital, and ending in bankruptcy, sorrow, and deprivation; the indefinite form magnifies or specifies the kind of loss.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r11.anchor: “Hüsr” ü “hüsran”, kazanacak yerde ziyan etmek, sermayeyi

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r12.claim: Life is humanity's capital: it is spent with every breath and hour, while accountability for this blessing approaches.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r12.anchor: Çünkü insanın sermayesi ömrüdür, o ise her nefes, her saat

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r13.claim: Life is a limited loan belonging to the Creator, entrusted to people to invest well; their benefit depends on the profit made by spending it.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r13.anchor: insanın kendi milki değil, yaratan Hâlık teâlâ’nın milki olup O’nun nâmına güzel tasarruf ederek

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r14.claim: A person receives only what they strive for and is held accountable for what they earn.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r14.anchor: İnsanın bütün istifadesi onun sarf u mübâdelesinden hâsıl olacak kâra bağlıdır

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r15.claim: After returning the loaned capital to its owner, people are saved and rewarded according to their profit or left liable, bankrupt, and punished according to their deficit; the scales express this reckoning.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r15.anchor: hesap günü kendisine kalacak olan kâra göre kendisini kurtaracak ve o nisbette mütena‘‘im olacak

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r16.claim: Every breath spent idly is loss; a worldly or neutral act leaves no lasting gain, evil is certainly loss, and even obedience could have been done better.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r16.anchor: Bir mubah ise bir eseri kalmamak itibariyle boşuna geçmiş gibidir. Bir şer ise muhakkak bir hüsrandır

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r17.claim: Because knowledge of Allah and His majesty can grow without limit, greater knowledge should produce deeper awe and love and more complete worship; settling for less entails some loss.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r17.anchor: insanın Allah’a ilmi ne kadar çok olursa haşyet ve mahabbeti de o nisbette çok

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r18.claim: Obstacles and constricting events that assail people compound the danger and loss inherent in the passing of time.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r18.anchor: asrın, zamanın cereyânı içinde her taraftan hücum etmekte bulunan mâni‘aları

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r19.claim: Even if people enjoyed constant comfort, their lives move toward death and each passing breath is itself a death.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r19.anchor: her dem ömrü ölüme doğru gitmekte bulunan insanın bir hüsran içinde bulunduğunu inkâr etmek kābil olmaz

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r20.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r20.claim: Razi says loss is humanity's basic condition: true happiness is loving the afterlife rather than attaching oneself to worldly pain and pleasure, yet most people pursue the world and are ruined.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r20.anchor: Bundan dolayı Râzî der ki: “Bu âyet insanda hüsran ve haybetin asl

ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r21.claim: Those with the four traits named in the next verse are exceptions to loss and instead gain.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#4/r21.anchor: Ancak o kimseler müstesnâ şu zikrolunacak dört vasıf ile muttasıf olanlar hüsranda değil, kârdadırlar

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r9.claim: Only those with faith, righteous works, mutual counsel in truth, and mutual counsel in patience are exceptions to humanity's otherwise absolute loss; all four express complete faith.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r9.anchor: ancak böyle iman, sâlih ameller, tevâsî bi’l-hak, tevâsî bi’s-sabr dört vasıf ile muttasıf olan kimseler hüsranda değil, müstesnâdırlar

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r10.claim: True faith in the real and abiding God cannot fail; a life spent in beautiful works for God is never wasted, while faith in falsehood and its deeds vanish.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r10.anchor: O’nun yolunda güzel amellere sarfedilmiş bulunan bir hayat, bir ömür hiçbir zaman boşa gitmez

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r11.claim: The verse implies that even people with true faith incur a kind of loss if they do not perform righteous deeds and counsel truth and patience.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r11.anchor: Hakk’a iman etmekle beraber sâlih ameller yapmayan ve hak ve sabır tavsiye etmeyen kimseler de bir nevi hüsrandan hâriç kalmamış olurlar

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r12.speaker: Mürcienin
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r12.claim: The Murji'a claim that lack of action causes no loss once faith exists is false; Ahl al-Sunna correctly holds that sinful, disobedient believers also incur a kind of loss.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r12.anchor: “iman olunca amelsizlik ziyan etmez” diyen Mürcienin kavilleri hak değildir. Doğrusu ehl-i sünnetin dedikleri gibi imanı olup da imanına göre âmil olmayan fâsıklar, âsîler için de bir nevi hüsran

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r13.claim: Although faith ultimately saves sinful believers, those whose sins outweigh their good deeds undergo Hell's loss until their sins are cleansed.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r13.anchor: seyyiâtı hasenâtından ağır gelen mü’minler de günahları temizlenene kadar cehennem azâbı olan hüsrânı göreceklerdir

ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.speaker: Ebû Medîne
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.claim: He reports that two of the Prophet's Companions would not part after meeting until they recited Sūrat al-ʿAṣr to each other and then exchanged greetings.
ELMALILI:103:1-3#6/r14.anchor: Ebû Medîne’den[^57]-ki sohbeti vardır- şöyle dediğini rivayet eylemişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.claim: God swears by this precious reality to stress time's value and warn that a person who fails to use it well ends in loss.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r6.anchor: zamanın önemine dikkat çekmiş; onu iyi değerlendirmeyen insanın sonunun

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r7.claim: Here, loss means the punishment of the hereafter, the greatest loss for someone who has wasted life and time, as Ibn Ashur is cited.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r7.anchor: Burada “ziyan”la âhiret azabı kastedilmiştir. Çünkü zamanı ve ömrü boşa geçirmiş insan için en büyük ziyan odur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.claim: Despite its brevity, Surah al-Asr contains a rich summary of the Qur'an's religious and moral duties and counsels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r17.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’deki bütün dinî ve ahlâkî yükümlülüklerin, öğütlerin özü sayılmaya değer

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.claim: Al-Shafi'i is quoted as saying that this short surah alone would suffice humanity if nothing else had been revealed, since it embraces all Qur'anic sciences.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r18.anchor: Şayet Kur’an’da başka bir şey nâzil olmasaydı, şu pek kısa sûre bile insanlara yeterdi. Bu sûre Kur’an’ın bütün ilimlerini kucaklıyor

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.speaker: Mehmet Âkif Ersoy
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.claim: Akif's poem presents true faith, righteous conduct, truth, and steadfastness as the sequence that saves humanity from loss.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:103:1/r19.anchor: Başta îmân-ı hakîkî geliyor sonra salâh Sonra hak sonra sebât: İşte kuzum insanlık Dördü birleşti mi yoktur sana hüsrân artık

BURSEVI:v10p390#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p390#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p390#3/r1.claim: The loss is grave because the servant sins against the Lord and against immense benefaction; the indefinite form may also mark a distinctive kind of loss beyond ordinary human usage.
BURSEVI:v10p390#3/r1.anchor: والذنب يعظم إما لعظم من في حقه الذنب أو لأنه في مقابلة النعمة العظيمة

QASHANI:103:3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:103:3/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:103:3/r3.claim: People are at loss through worldly pleasures and time's veil, wasting the lasting capital of innate guidance and primordial potential.
QASHANI:103:3/r3.anchor: على أن المحجوب به عنه في خسر وهو الإنسان لخسارته برأس ماله الذي هو نور الفطرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r1.claim: The exception completes the division into those who lose and those untouched by loss; believers who do good avoid loss if they leave no good undone by committing its opposite, or repent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r1.anchor: فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لا يلحقهم الخسران بحال إذا لم يتركوا شيئا من الصالحات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r3.claim: Loss has degrees: eternal loss comes from denying God's oneness and the Messenger; lesser loss varies with evil deeds, and minor sins may be forgiven when major sins are avoided, as in 11:114.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r3.anchor: فأعظمه وخالده الخسر المنجر عن انتفاء الإيمان بوحدانية الله وصدق الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r4.claim: The loss is in the future life, as the warning context indicates, regardless of worldly fortunes; compare 3:196–197.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r4.anchor: أي لفي خسر في الحياة الأبدية الآخرة فلا التفات إلى أحوال الناس في الحياة الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r5.claim: The indefinite khusr can indicate kinds of loss or intensify and universalize it for dramatic effect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r5.anchor: وتنكير { خسر } يجوز أن يكون للتنويع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r6.claim: Al-ṣāliḥāt is generic yet comprehensive of every commanded good deed, including avoiding sins; the exception's relative clause states why they are spared loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p531/r6.anchor: والتعريف في قوله : { الصالحات } تعريف الجنس مراد به الاستغراق

QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.claim: The generic definite al-nafs parallels generic human statements qualified by exceptions; the verse forbids killing any protected life, Muslim or treaty-holder, except for a legally valid cause.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:151#3/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية نهي عن قتل النفس المحرمة، مؤمنة كانت أو معاهدة إلا بالحق

TABATABAI:103:3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:103:3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:103:3/r3.claim: A report interprets the human in loss as Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and identifies Ali and Salman among those who believe and do good.
TABATABAI:103:3/r3.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عباس في قوله

TABRISI:103:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:103:3/r7.claim: Humanity is in loss because lifespan diminishes daily; without earning obedience through it, people incur the greatest loss, permanent punishment.
TABRISI:103:3/r7.anchor: أنه لفي نقصان لأنه ينقص عمره كل يوم وهو رأس ماله

TABRISI:103:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r8.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:103:3/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash says the loss means destruction.

TABRISI:103:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:103:3/r9.claim: Another view takes loss as punishment and deprivation of one's allotted opportunity and home in Paradise.
TABRISI:103:3/r9.anchor: معناه لفي عقوبة وغبن من فوت أمهله ومنزله في الجنة

TABRISI:103:3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:103:3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:103:3/r10.claim: “Humanity” may mean disbelievers specifically, such as Abū Jahl and al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
TABRISI:103:3/r10.anchor: المراد بالإنسان الكافر خاصة وهو أبو جهل والوليد بن المغيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited as mentioning ʿAlī and Salmān among those described as saved, and Abū Jahl as an example of the losing human; Alusi says neither example is exclusive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p228#3/r3.anchor: اقتصار ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما في الذكر عليهما

BINTSHATI:v2p86/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r1.claim: Against al-Nīsābūrī, the indefinite form khusr is not simply an intensifier; she reads it as open-ended and unrestricted.
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r1.anchor: المبالغات كما ذهب النيسابورى. وإنما التنكير

BINTSHATI:v2p86/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r2.claim: Indefiniteness may also convey awe, as al-Rāzī suggests: the loss is so great that only God comprehends it.
BINTSHATI:v2p86/r2.anchor: على ما قال الرازي. ووجهه عنده

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r5.claim: Loss means deficiency; the believers who believe, do good, and counsel truth and patience are not diminished.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p204#2/r5.anchor: والخسر: النقصان إلا الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1.claim: She questions the link between the supposed greatness of night and day and the claim that human striving differs, and between the falling star and the assertion that the Prophet is neither astray nor deluded.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p245/r1.anchor: بين: إن سعيكم لشتى؟ أو بين عظمة النجم إذا هوى، و {مَا ضَلَّ صَاحِبُكُمْ وَمَا غَوَى} ؟

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur announces that the Quran has distinctive stylistic innovations which he proceeds to enumerate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r1.anchor: هذا وللقرآن مبتكرات تميز بها نظمه عن بقية كلام العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r2.claim: The Quran departs from both poetry and ordinary oratory, using a novel form of a book meant to be preserved and recited; this is one aspect of its inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r2.anchor: فمنها أنه جاء على أسلوب يخالف الشعر لا محالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r3.claim: Quranic sentences state carefully delimited propositions and rules rather than loose generalities or unrestricted statements, unlike Arab usage that often ignored rare cases.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r3.anchor: جاء بالجمل الدالة على معان مفيدة محررة شأن الجمل العلمية والقواعد التشريعية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r6.claim: The declaration that humanity is in loss is explicitly qualified by the following exception for believers, exemplifying precise wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r6.anchor: إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r7.claim: The Quran introduced systematic division and topic classification into Arabic discourse, a practice al-Kashshaf had hinted at.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r7.anchor: طريقة التبويب والتصنيف وقد أومأ إليها في الكشاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r8.claim: Quranic narrative vividly depicts paradise, punishment, and states of affairs; this strongly affected Arabs because narrative was nearly absent from Arabic literature, apart from rare poetic episodes such as al-Nabigha's snake story.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r8.anchor: وقد كان لذلك تأثير عظيم على نفوس العرب إذ كان فن القصص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r9.claim: The Quran reshapes reported speech into its own miraculous Arabic style; reported words convey meaning rather than exact wording, so the inimitability belongs to the Quran, not the quoted speakers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r9.anchor: فهو إذا حكى أقوالا غير عربية صاغ مدلولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r10.claim: The Quran also adapts names in its narratives for eloquence, changing Saul to Talut and Terah, Abraham's father, to Azar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p120/r10.anchor: ومن هذا القبيل حكاية الأسماء الواقعة في القصص فإن القرآن يغيرها إلى ما يناسب حسن مواقعها في الكلام

BURHAN:v4p88/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p88/r1.speaker: ابن بابشاذ
BURHAN:v4p88/r1.claim: Ibn Babshadh says the definite article of specific reference concerns what is established in external entities, while the generic article concerns what is established in the mind; external instances match the mental universal.
BURHAN:v4p88/r1.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن بابشاذ إن تعريف العهد لما ثبت في الاعيان وتعريف الجنس لما ثبت في الاذهان

BURHAN:v4p88/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p88/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p88/r2.claim: The fourth use denotes a universal essence: replacing the article with 'all' preserves its literal sense and entails exhaustive reference; the valid exception in 103:2 and plural description demonstrate this.
BURHAN:v4p88/r2.anchor: الرابع إن يقصد بها الحقيقة باعتبار كلية ذلك المعنى وتعرف بانها التي اذا نزعت حسن إن يخلفها كل

BURHAN:v4p88/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p88/r3.speaker: صاحب ضوء المصباح
BURHAN:v4p88/r3.claim: The scope may be genus or species: an article attached to an action marks a species whose name ceases when the action stops, while one attached to a quality marks a lasting genus.
BURHAN:v4p88/r3.anchor: قال صاحب ضوء المصباح ( 3 ) سواء أكان الشمول باعتبار الجنس

BURHAN:v4p88/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p88/r4.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين الرازي ومن تبعه
BURHAN:v4p88/r4.claim: Fakhr al-Din and his followers deny that a singular noun made definite by alif-lam is general.
BURHAN:v4p88/r4.anchor: خلافا للامام فخر الدين ومن تبعه في قولهم إن المفرد المحلي بالالف واللام لايعم

BURHAN:v4p88/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p88/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p88/r5.claim: The author rejects that denial: the exception in 103:2 proves generality; the thief wording does not prove it by itself, but denotes the essence of theft, applying to every thief across time.

BURHAN:v4p88/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p88/r6.speaker: العلماء
BURHAN:v4p88/r6.claim: Scholars disagree whether the definite article on a plural removes its plural force to make it generic and singular, or leaves the plural meaning intact.
BURHAN:v4p88/r6.anchor: فان دخلت على جمع فاختلف العلماء هل سلبته معنى الجمع ويصير للجنس

BURHAN:v2p7/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p7/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p7/r1.claim: The definite singular in 103:2 is generic, illustrating how alif-lām gives a singular noun universal scope.
BURHAN:v2p7/r1.anchor: ويستفاد عموم المفرد المحلى باللام من قوله ﴿ إن الإنسان لفي خسر ﴾

BURHAN:v2p232/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p232/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p232/r1.claim: A singular address such as “O human” can address all people; the exception “except those who believe” confirms the universal sense of al-insān in 103:2.
BURHAN:v2p232/r1.anchor: والمراد الجميع بدليل قوله ﴿ إن الإنسان لفي خسر إلا الذين آمنوا ﴾

BURHAN:v2p232/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p232/r2.speaker: الحجاج
BURHAN:v2p232/r2.claim: Al-Ḥajjāj used “O human” in a sermon and explained that every listener was that human.
BURHAN:v2p232/r2.anchor: وكان الحجاج يقول في خطبته يأيها الإنسان وكلكم ذلك الإنسان

ITQAN:v4p353/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p353/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p353/r5.claim: A fifth pattern pairs an oath with a proposition about human action or condition; al-ʿAsr exemplifies it by declaring humanity in loss.

ITQAN:v2p439/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p439/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p439/r1.claim: Al before active and passive participles can be a relative pronoun meaning who or that; other analyses call it a definite article or a relative particle.
ITQAN:v2p439/r1.anchor: أحدها أن تكون اسما موصولا بمعنى الذي وفروعه وهي الداخلة على أسماء الفاعلين والمفعولين

ITQAN:v2p439/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p439/r2.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v2p439/r2.claim: Alternative analyses treat this al as a definite article or a relative particle.
ITQAN:v2p439/r2.anchor: وقيل هي حينئذ حرف تعريف وقيل موصول حرفي

ITQAN:v2p439/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p439/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p439/r3.claim: Anaphoric al has verbal, mental, and present-context antecedents; verbal reference can point to an earlier noun.
ITQAN:v2p439/r3.anchor: فالعهدية إما أن يكون مصحوبها معهودا ذكريا

ITQAN:v2p439/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p439/r4.speaker: ابن عصفور
ITQAN:v2p439/r4.claim: Ibn Asfur also classifies al after a demonstrative, vocative أي, sudden إذ, or a present-time noun such as الآن as anaphoric.
ITQAN:v2p439/r4.anchor: قال ابن عصفور وكذا كل واقعة بعد اسم الإشارة أو أي في النداء وإذا الفجائية أو في اسم الزمان الحاضر نحو الآن

ITQAN:v2p439/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p439/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p439/r5.claim: Generic al can denote every individual; exception and plural description support that reading, so al-insan in 103:2 means every human.
ITQAN:v2p439/r5.anchor: والجنسية إما لاستغراق الأفراد وهي التي تخلفها كل حقيقة

ITQAN:v2p439/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p439/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p439/r6.claim: Generic al can instead encompass all the qualities of a class; al-kitab in that Book means the complete, guidance-rich Book.
ITQAN:v2p439/r6.anchor: وإما لاستغراق خصائص الأفراد وهي التي تخلفها كل مجازا

ITQAN:v2p439/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p439/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p439/r7.claim: Generic al can define essence or genus without meaning every; unlike an indefinite noun, it presents the truth as mentally specified.
ITQAN:v2p439/r7.anchor: وإما لتعريف الماهية والحقيقة والجنس وهي التي لا تخلفها كل لا حقيقة ولا مجازا

ITQAN:v3p41/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p41/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p41/r1.claim: A general expression covers all instances without restriction; كل can occur initially or after its noun.
ITQAN:v3p41/r1.anchor: العام لفظ يستغرق الصالح له من غير حصر وصيغته ( كل ) مبتدأة

ITQAN:v3p41/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p41/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p41/r2.claim: Relative pronouns in singular, dual, and plural forms can be general, covering anyone who fits the description.

ITQAN:v3p41/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p41/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p41/r3.claim: أي, ما, and من are general when used as conditionals, questions, or relative pronouns.
ITQAN:v3p41/r3.anchor: وأي وما ومن شرطا واستفهاما وموصولا نحو

ITQAN:v3p41/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p41/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p41/r4.claim: General forms include a plural in a possessive construction and nouns marked definite with al.
ITQAN:v3p41/r4.anchor: ﴿ يوصيكم الله في أولادكم ﴾ والمعرف بأل نحو

ITQAN:v3p41/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p41/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p41/r5.claim: A singular noun in a possessive construction can also be general; أمره means every command of God.
ITQAN:v3p41/r5.anchor: واسم الجنس المضاف نحو ﴿ فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره ﴾ أي كل أمر الله

ITQAN:v3p41/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p41/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p41/r6.claim: Definite al can be general: al-bay means every sale, and al-insan in 103:2 means every human, as the exception shows.
ITQAN:v3p41/r6.anchor: والمعرف بأل نحو ﴿ وأحل الله البيع ﴾ أي كل بيع

ITQAN:v3p41/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p41/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p41/r7.claim: Indefinite nouns become general in negation or prohibition, conditional clauses, and expressions of divine favor.
ITQAN:v3p41/r7.anchor: والنكرة في سياق النفي والنهي نحو

ITQAN:v3p58/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p58/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p58/r5.claim: The exception in 103:3 specifies the general statement in 103:2; Ibn al-Arabi is praised for distinguishing specification from abrogation.
ITQAN:v3p58/r5.anchor: وقد اعتنى ابن العربي بتحريره فأجاد كقوله

ITQAN:v3p103/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p103/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p103/r8.claim: The same substitution pattern uses a report for what is reported, desire for its object, and saying for what was said.
ITQAN:v3p103/r8.anchor: ومنها إطلاق البشرى على المبشر به والهوى على المهوي والقول على المقول

ITQAN:v3p103/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p103/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p103/r15.claim: The singular الإنسان can mean all people; the exception of believers confirms its plural sense.
ITQAN:v3p103/r15.anchor: وعلى الجمع نحو ﴿ إن الإنسان لفي خسر ﴾ أي الأناسي بدليل الإستثناء منه

DAMGHANI:v1p155/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p155/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p155/r9.claim: Khusr can mean misguidance; the verse says humanity is in misguidance.

DAMGHANI:v1p155/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p155/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p155/r10.claim: The five-sense heading also lists decrease and punishment as further senses of khusr, but this extract ends before their examples.
DAMGHANI:v1p155/r10.anchor: خ س ر على خمسة أوجه العجز الغبن الضلال النقص العقوبة فوجه منها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r10.claim: The source identifies the الإنسان who is in loss as Abū Lahab ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p181/r10.anchor: والرابع والعشرون : أبو لهب بن عبد العزى بن عبد المطلب [ ومنه ] قوله تعالى في العصر : ﴿ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r1.claim: Khusrān means loss or diminution; conventionally it is a reduction in one's capital.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r1.anchor: الخسران : النقص . وهو في التعارف نقص جزء من رأس المال

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r5.claim: For the oath in al-ʿAṣr, khusr means misguidance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p277/r5.anchor: والرابع : الضلال : ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء : ﴿ فقد خسر خسرانا مبينا ﴾

IBNASHUR:103:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:2/r1.claim: Al-insan is a generic definite with customary comprehensive force: people living when Islam appeared, especially those reached by its call across the world; after the exception of believers who do good, the judgment remains true of others.

IBNASHUR:103:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:2/r2.claim: Loss, the opposite of profit in trade, is a metaphor for the bad afterlife outcome of someone who expects a good end, whether bliss or punishment; it echoes the cited verse about an unprofitable trade.
IBNASHUR:103:2/r2.anchor: مصدر وهو ضد الربح في التجارة

IBNASHUR:103:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:2/r3.claim: The phrase in loss uses figurative containment: being enclosed by loss is stronger than simply calling a person a loser.
IBNASHUR:103:2/r3.anchor: شبهت ملازمة الخسر بإحاطة الظرف بالمظروف

IBNASHUR:103:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:2/r4.claim: The universal assertion, strengthened by the oath and emphatic particle, warns of the condition enveloping most people.
IBNASHUR:103:2/r4.anchor: يفيد التهويل والإنذار بالحالة المحيطة بمعظم الناس

KASHSHAF:103:2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:103:2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:103:2/r1.claim: Al-insān refers to humanity as a class.

KASHSHAF:103:2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:103:2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:103:2/r2.claim: Khusr means loss, just as kufr can mean kufrān.
KASHSHAF:103:2/r2.anchor: والخسر : الخسران ،   كما قيل : الكفر في الكفران

RAZI:103:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r1.claim: The definite article in الإنسان may refer to humanity as a class or to a previously known individual.
RAZI:103:2/r1.anchor: الألف واللام في الإنسان ، يحتمل أن تكون للجنس

RAZI:103:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r2.claim: On the generic reading, the verse means humanity generally is in loss, as the following exception for believers indicates.
RAZI:103:2/r2.anchor: أن المراد منه الجنس وهو كقولهم : كثر الدرهم في أيدي الناس

RAZI:103:2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:103:2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies a specific group of polytheists: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Waʾil, and al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
RAZI:103:2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد جماعة من المشركين كالوليد بن المغيرة

RAZI:103:2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:103:2/r4.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about Abu Lahab.
RAZI:103:2/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في أبي لهب

RAZI:103:2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r5.speaker: خبر مرفوع
RAZI:103:2/r5.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet identifies the person as Abu Jahl; no grading is stated.
RAZI:103:2/r5.anchor: وفي خبر مرفوع إنه أبو جهل

RAZI:103:2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r6.claim: A report says these people used to claim Muhammad was in loss, so God swore that the opposite was true.
RAZI:103:2/r6.anchor: وروي أن هؤلاء كانوا يقولون : إن محمدا لفي خسر

RAZI:103:2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r7.claim: خسر means loss or decrease, like خسران and كفران, and can mean losing one’s capital.

RAZI:103:2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r8.claim: If الإنسان is generic, loss means wasting one’s self and lifetime, except for believers who gain everlasting bliss through them.
RAZI:103:2/r8.anchor: إذا حملنا الإنسان على الجنس كان معنى الخسر هلاك نفسه وعمره

RAZI:103:2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r9.claim: If الإنسان means unbelievers, loss is error and disbelief, from which those who believe escape into profit.
RAZI:103:2/r9.anchor: وإن حملنا لفظ الإنسان على الكافر كان المراد كونه في الضلالة والكفر

RAZI:103:2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r10.claim: The indefinite خسر may magnify the loss: it is immense beyond human comprehension because sin is against God and against great blessings.
RAZI:103:2/r10.anchor: فإن حملنا على الأول كان المعنى إن الإنسان لفي خسر عظيم لا يعلم كنهه إلا الله

RAZI:103:2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r11.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite may belittle the loss by implying human loss is less than Satan’s, a consoling reminder that someone is more disobedient.
RAZI:103:2/r11.anchor: وإن حملناه على الثاني كان المعنى أن خسران الإنسان دون خسران الشيطان

RAZI:103:2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r12.claim: The author says the magnifying interpretation is the correct one.

RAZI:103:2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r13.claim: Although الإنسان is involved in many losses, the singular wording points to the true loss: deprivation of serving God; loss of Paradise and punishment are negligible by comparison.
RAZI:103:2/r13.anchor: أن الخسر الحقيقي هو حرمانه عن خدمة ربه

RAZI:103:2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r14.claim: The purpose of creation is worship, so all other purposes are negligible by comparison.
RAZI:103:2/r14.anchor: ثم قال : { وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون } أي لما كان هذا المقصود أجل المقاصد

RAZI:103:2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r15.claim: The emphatic إن and lām, together with في, portray a person immersed and surrounded by loss.
RAZI:103:2/r15.anchor: قوله : { لفي خسر } يفيد أنه كالمغمور في الخسران ، وأنه أحاط به من كل جانب

RAZI:103:2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r16.claim: The particle إن adds emphasis to the assertion of loss.

RAZI:103:2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r17.claim: One construal takes في خسر as being on the path to loss, as with consuming an orphan’s wealth “in their bellies” when the outcome is Fire.
RAZI:103:2/r17.anchor: في قوله تعالى : { لفي خسر } أي في طريق الخسر ، وهذا كقوله في أكل أموال اليتامى

RAZI:103:2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r18.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r18.claim: Another construal says no person escapes loss because life is capital that is continually spent.
RAZI:103:2/r18.anchor: أن الإنسان لا ينفك عن خسر ، لأن الخسر هو تضييع رأس المال

RAZI:103:2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r19.claim: Every hour spent in sin is loss; even permissible activity loses time without lasting effect, although it could have been used for enduring work.
RAZI:103:2/r19.anchor: فإن كانت مصروفة إلى المعصية فلا شك في الخسران ، وإن كانت مشغولة بالمباحات

RAZI:103:2/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r20.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r20.claim: Even worship can fall short: devotion has endlessly higher degrees as knowledge of God’s majesty grows, so settling for a lower degree is a kind of loss.
RAZI:103:2/r20.anchor: مراتب الخضوع والخشوع لله غير متناهية

RAZI:103:2/r21.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r21.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r21.claim: Humanity tends toward loss because afterlife-directed motives are hidden while worldly motives—senses, desire, and anger—are obvious, leaving most people absorbed in the world.
RAZI:103:2/r21.anchor: وتقريره أن سعادة الإنسان في حب الآخرة والإعراض عن الدنيا ، ثم إن الأسباب الداعية إلى الآخرة خفية

RAZI:103:2/r22.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:103:2/r22.speaker: author
RAZI:103:2/r22.claim: The apparent contrast with Surah al-Tin is resolved by distinguishing bodily conditions there from the soul’s conditions here.
RAZI:103:2/r22.anchor: قلنا : المذكور في سورة التين أحوال البدن ، وههنا أحوال النفس فلا تناقض بين القولين

KASHSHAF:103:3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:103:3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:103:3/r1.claim: Everyone loses in trade except the righteous, who buy the afterlife with the world and gain happiness; all who trade in the opposite way lose and suffer.
KASHSHAF:103:3/r1.anchor: أن الناس في خسران من تجارتهم إلا الصالحين وحدهم

TAB:103:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:2/r1.speaker: author
TAB:103:2/r1.claim: The human being, meaning the children of Adam, is in ruin and diminishment.
TAB:103:2/r1.anchor: يقول :  إن ابن آدم لفي هلكة ونقصان

TAB:103:2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:2/r2.speaker: علي
TAB:103:2/r2.claim: A reported reading from ʿAlī expands the oath to “the vicissitudes of time” and adds that humanity remains in loss until the end of time.
TAB:103:2/r2.anchor: قال :  سمعت عليا رضي الله عنه يقرأ هذا الحرف :  «والعصر ونوائب الدهر ،   إن الإنسان لفي خسر ،   وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر »

TAB:103:2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB:103:2/r3.claim: Qatada says some readings add that humanity remains in loss until the end of time.
TAB:103:2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {  إن الإنسان لفي خسر } ففي بعض القراءات :  «وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر »

TAB:103:2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:103:2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:103:2/r4.claim: Mujahid explains the loss as applying to everyone except those who believe.
TAB:103:2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {  إن الإنسان لفي خسر } إلا من آمن

ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r1.claim: Al-ʿaṣr and al-insān are generic nouns, so the exception in the next verse can validly be taken from them.
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r1.anchor: والعصر والإنسان اسم جنس يعم ،   ولذلك صح الاستثناء منه

ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r2.claim: Khusr means loss, as kufr is related to kufrān.

ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r3.claim: No loss is greater than losing both this world and the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r3.anchor: وأي خسران أعظم ممن خسر الدنيا والآخرة

ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r4.speaker: ابن هرمز وزيد بن علي وهارون عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r4.claim: Ibn Hurmuz, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and Hārūn from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read khusr with a ḍamma on sīn; the majority use sukūn.
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز وزيد بن علي وهارون عن أبي بكر عن عاصم : خسر بضم السين ،   والجمهور بالسكون

ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r5.claim: Whoever sells the afterlife for this world suffers the utmost loss, unlike the believer who buys the afterlife with this world and thereby profits and prospers.
ABUHAYYAN:103:2/r5.anchor: ومن باع آخرته بدنياه فهو في غاية الخسران ،   بخلاف المؤمن ،   فإنه اشترى الآخرة بالدنيا ،   فربح وسعد

ALUSI:103:1/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:1/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:1/r19.claim: The oath recalls time's blessings and opposites, but the next verse assigns loss to people, not time; this rebuts blaming time for events, though using ʿaṣr for dahr seems unclear.
ALUSI:103:1/r19.anchor: وفي إضافة الخسران بعد ذلك للإنسان اشعار بأنه صفة له لا للزمان

ALUSI:103:2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:2/r1.claim: People lose through trades, efforts, and spending their lives on aims that bring no afterlife benefit and may harm them at resurrection.
ALUSI:103:2/r1.anchor: أي خسران في متاجرهم ومساعيهم وصرف أعمارهم في مباغيهم التي لا ينتفعون بها في الآخرة

ALUSI:103:2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:2/r2.claim: Al-insān is definite in the generic sense, as shown by the exception that follows.

ALUSI:103:2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:2/r3.claim: The indefinite khusr may magnify the loss as immense, or indicate a particular kind of loss unfamiliar to people.
ALUSI:103:2/r3.anchor: والتنكير قيل للتعظيم أي في خسر عظيم ويجوز أن يكون للتنويع

ALUSI:103:3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r13.speaker: علي
ALUSI:103:3/r13.claim: A report attributes to ʿAlī a reading adding nawāʾib al-dahr and extending the loss statement to the end of time.
ALUSI:103:3/r13.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه كان يقرى والعصر ونوائب الدهر إن الإنسان لفي خسر

ALUSI:103:3/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r14.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
ALUSI:103:3/r14.claim: Maymūn ibn Mihrān reports a reading ascribed to Ibn Masʿūd that says the person remains in loss until the end of time, except those who believe.
ALUSI:103:3/r14.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران أنه قرأ والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر وإنه لفيه إلى آخر الدهر

ALUSI:103:3/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI:103:3/r16.claim: Al-Ālūsī replies that the verse puts everyone outside the exception in loss, not necessarily eternal Hell: loss may mean Hell for an unpardoned sinner or missed highest ranks if forgiven.
ALUSI:103:3/r16.anchor: وأما على كونه مخلداً في النار فلا كيف والخسر عام

ALUSI:103:3/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:103:3/r17.speaker: الماتريدي
ALUSI:103:3/r17.claim: Al-Māturīdī offers further ways to answer the objection in al-Taʾwīlāt, but al-Ālūsī calls them strained.
ALUSI:103:3/r17.anchor: وللشيخ الماتريدي رحمه الله تعالى في التفصي عن ذلك تكلفات مذكورة في التأويلات

BAGHAWI:103:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:103:2/r1.anchor: أي خسران ونقصان ، قيل : أراد به الكفار

BAGHAWI:103:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:103:2/r2.claim: One view takes “humanity” here to mean the unbelievers, since believers are excepted afterward.
BAGHAWI:103:2/r2.anchor: قيل : أراد به الكفار ، بدليل أنه استثنى المؤمنين

BAGHAWI:103:2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:103:2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:103:2/r3.claim: Loss is a person’s capital being squandered as sin destroys the self and lifespan, humanity’s two greatest assets.
BAGHAWI:103:2/r3.anchor: والخسران : ذهاب رأس مال الإنسان في هلاك نفسه وعمره بالمعاصي ، وهما أكبر رأس ماله

BAYDAWI:103:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:103:1/r4.claim: The oath indirectly denies that loss is attributable to time.
BAYDAWI:103:1/r4.anchor: والتعريض بنفي ما يضاف إليه من الخسران

BAYDAWI:103:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:103:2/r1.claim: People lose in their endeavors and in spending their lifetimes pursuing their aims.
BAYDAWI:103:2/r1.anchor: إن الناس لفي خسران في مساعيهم ، وصرف أعمارهم في مطالبهم

BAYDAWI:103:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:103:2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:103:2/r2.claim: The definite article is generic, while the indefinite form magnifies the loss.

BIQAI:103:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:2/r1.claim: Humanity is the noblest species because it was made in the best form; al-ʿaṣr is the essence of time, and the root also evokes extracting essences.
BIQAI:103:2/r1.anchor: أي هذا النوع الذي هو أشرف الأنواع ، لكونه في أحسن تقويم ، كما أن العصر خلاصة الزمان ، والعصر يكون لاستخراج خلاصات الأشياء

BIQAI:103:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:2/r2.claim: Loss is deficiency from pursuing whims and spending one's time on personal aims, driven by attachment to the present and delusion by what passes away.
BIQAI:103:2/r2.anchor: أي نقص بحسب مساعيهم في أهوائهم ، وصرف أعصارهم في أغراضهم ، لما لهم بالطبع من الميل إلى الحاضر ، والإعراض عن الغائب ، والاغترار بالفاني

BIQAI:103:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:2/r3.claim: Loss ranges from slight to grave: unbelievers are in ingratitude, while sinful believers face loss proportionate to their disobedience, at least in the unqualified sense.
BIQAI:103:2/r3.anchor: أعم من أن يكون الخسر قليلاً أو جليلاً بحسب تنوع الناس إلى أكياس وأرجاس ، فمن كان كافراً كان في كفران ، ومن كان مؤمناً عاصياً كان في خسران

BIQAI:103:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:103:2/r4.claim: Human need for messengers follows: they explain which beliefs, worship, and customs please God, so people can persist in faith and Islam.
BIQAI:103:2/r4.anchor: وفي هذا إشارة إلى العلم بالاحتياج إلى إرسال الرسل لبيان المرضي لله من الاعتقادات والعبادات والعادات إيماناً وإسلاماً

BIQAI:103:2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:103:2/r5.speaker: الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:103:2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects this universal loss to al-Takāthur's short-sightedness, humanity's innate injustice and ignorance in 33:72, and the exception whose trade never distracts them in 24:37.
BIQAI:103:2/r5.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : لما قال تعالى : { ألهاكم التكاثر } وتضمن ذلك الإشارة إلى قصور نظر الإنسان

DURR:103:1/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r2.speaker: أبو مليكة الدارمي
DURR:103:1/r2.claim: Abū Mulayka al-Dārimī, a Companion, says two Companions would not part after meeting until one recited the whole sūra to the other, then they exchanged greetings.
DURR:103:1/r2.anchor: عن أبي مليكة الدارمي- وكانت له صحبة- قال : كان الرجلان من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:103:1/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:103:1/r4.claim: ʿAlī is reported to have read “by time and the calamities of time,” then added that humanity remains in loss to time’s end.
DURR:103:1/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب أنه كان يقرأ «والعصر ونوائب الدهر

DURR:103:1/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:103:1/r5.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr recited the reading attributed to Ibn Masʿūd with the addition “he is in it until the end of time” before the exception.
DURR:103:1/r5.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن عبد الملك قال : سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقرأ قراءة ابن مسعود

DURR:103:1/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR:103:1/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm says they recited the expanded “until the end of time” wording and identifies it as part of ʿAbd Allāh b. Masʿūd’s reading.
DURR:103:1/r6.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال : قرأنا «والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر

DURR:103:1/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود
DURR:103:1/r7.claim: Ḥawshab reports that ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUtba described Ibn Masʿūd’s reading as saying humanity remains in loss until time’s end.
DURR:103:1/r7.anchor: عن حوشب قال : أرسل بشر بن مروان إلى عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود فقال

DURR:103:1/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r8.speaker: بشر بن مروان
DURR:103:1/r8.claim: Bishr b. Marwān called the expanded reading disbelief.
DURR:103:1/r8.anchor: فقال له بشر : هو يكفر به .

DURR:103:1/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:103:1/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود
DURR:103:1/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿUtba rejects Bishr’s accusation, saying he believes the expanded reading.
DURR:103:1/r9.anchor: فقال عبد الله ، لكني أومن به .

IBNASHUR:103:3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r5.claim: The warning concerns the future, especially the eternal afterlife, and should not be judged by worldly turns of fortune.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r5.anchor: وهذا الخبر مراد به الحصول في المستقبل بقرينة مقام الإنذار والوعيد

IBNASHUR:103:3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r6.claim: The indefinite form of loss may indicate kinds of loss, or magnification and comprehensiveness in the oath's threatening context.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r6.anchor: وتنكير { خسر } يجوز أن يكون للتنويع

IBNASHUR:103:3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:103:3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:103:3/r7.claim: The author glosses the people in great loss as the polytheists.
IBNASHUR:103:3/r7.anchor: إن الناس لفي خسران عظيم وهم المشركون

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r1.claim: Al-insan is the generic human species; khusr means loss, decline, and a bad state.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r1.anchor: و { الإنسان } اسم الجنس ، و «الخسر » : النقصان وسوء الحال

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r2.claim: The clearest instance is the disbeliever, who loses this world and the next, which is manifest loss.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r2.anchor: وذلك بين غاية البيان في الكافر ؛ لأنه خسر الدنيا والآخرة

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r3.claim: A believer may lose through old age and worldly hardship, but that is forgiven beside everlasting success and profit in the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r3.anchor: وأما المؤمن وإن كان في خسر دنياه في هرمه وما يقاسيه من شقاء هذه الدار

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r5.claim: Ali is reported to read the opening as By the vicissitudes of time, mankind is in loss.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r5.anchor: وقرأ علي بن أبي طالب : «والعصر ونوائب الدهر إن الإنسان »

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r6.speaker: عبد الله
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r6.claim: Abdullah’s codex has By time, We created mankind in loss.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r6.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله : «والعصر لقد خلقنا الإنسان في خسر »

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r7.claim: Ali is also reported to add that mankind remains in loss until the end of time, except those who believe.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r7.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب أنه قرأ «إن الإنسان لفي خسر وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر إلا الذين »

IBNATIYYA:103:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r8.speaker: عاصم والأعرج
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r8.claim: Asim and al-Araj read khusr with a damma on the sīn.
IBNATIYYA:103:2/r8.anchor: وقرأ عاصم والأعرج : «لفي خسُر » بضم السين

IBNATIYYA:103:3/r8.anchor: وقرأ عاصم والأعرج : «لفي خسُر » بضم السين

IBNKATHIR:103:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:103:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:103:1/r2.claim: A report places Amr b. al-As with Musaylima after Muhammad's mission but before Amr's conversion: Musaylima asks what was revealed, Amr recites al-Asr, Musaylima offers nonsense verse, and Amr calls him a liar.
IBNKATHIR:103:1/r2.anchor: ذكروا أن عمرو بن العاص وفد على مسيلمة الكذاب

MAWARDI:103:2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:103:2/r1.claim: Al-insan refers to people as a species, humankind generally.

MAWARDI:103:2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:2/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:103:2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi glosses khusr as ruin or destruction.

MAWARDI:103:2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:2/r3.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI:103:2/r3.claim: Zayd b. Aslam glosses khusr as evil.
MAWARDI:103:2/r3.anchor: الثاني : لفي شر ، قاله زيد بن أسلم .

MAWARDI:103:2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:2/r4.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI:103:2/r4.claim: Ibn Shajara glosses khusr as loss or decrease.
MAWARDI:103:2/r4.anchor: الثالث : لفي نقص ، قاله ابن شجرة .

MAWARDI:103:2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI:103:2/r5.claim: A fourth sense is punishment, supported by the phrase “the consequence of its affair was loss” in 65:9.
MAWARDI:103:2/r5.anchor: الرابع : لفي عقوبة ، ومنه قوله تعالى : { وكان عاقبة أمرها خُسْراً }

MAWARDI:103:2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:103:2/r6.speaker: علي
MAWARDI:103:2/r6.claim: ʿAli is reported to gloss the oath as the age and the vicissitudes of time, adding that humankind remains in loss until the end of time.
MAWARDI:103:2/r6.anchor: وكان عليّ رضي الله عنه يقرؤها : ( والعصر ونوائب الدهر إنّ الإنسان لفي خسر وإنه فيه إلى آخر الدهر )

NASAFI:103:2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:103:2/r1.claim: The oath's response says humanity as a species is in loss through its transactions.
NASAFI:103:2/r1.anchor: أي جنس الإنسان لفي خسران من تجاراتهم

QURTUBI:103:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:103:2/r1.claim: This verse is the answer to the oath.

QURTUBI:103:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:103:2/r2.claim: In a report through Abū Ṣāliḥ, Ibn ʿAbbās says “the human” means the unbeliever.
QURTUBI:103:2/r2.anchor: والمراد به الكافر ،   قاله ابن عباس في رواية أبي صالح

QURTUBI:103:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r3.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI:103:2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits that the verse targets a group of polytheists, including al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra and al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil.
QURTUBI:103:2/r3.anchor: وروى الضحاك عنه قال : يريد جماعة من المشركين : الوليد بن المغيرة

QURTUBI:103:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:103:2/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes al-insān to mean humankind as a whole; verse 3’s exception confirms this as the sound reading.
QURTUBI:103:2/r4.anchor: وقيل : يعني بالإنسان جنس الناس .   { لفي خسر } لفي غبن

QURTUBI:103:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:103:2/r5.claim: Khusr means loss; al-Akhfash glosses it as destruction, al-Farrāʾ as punishment, Ibn Zayd as evil, and another view as deficiency, all close in meaning.
QURTUBI:103:2/r5.anchor: لفي غبن .   وقال الأخفش : هلكة .   الفراء : عقوبة

QURTUBI:103:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI:103:2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses khusr as evil; another view calls it deficiency.
QURTUBI:103:2/r6.anchor: ابن زيد : لفي شر .   وقيل : لفي نقص .   المعنى متقارب

QURTUBI:103:2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r8.speaker: الأعرج وطلحة وعيسى الثقفي
QURTUBI:103:2/r8.claim: Al-Aʿraj, Ṭalḥa, and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read khusr with ḍamma on sīn; Hārūn transmits it from Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim, with vowel-following as the basis for the variants.
QURTUBI:103:2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج وطلحة وعيسى الثقفي " خسر " بضم السين

QURTUBI:103:2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r9.speaker: علي
QURTUBI:103:2/r9.claim: A recitation attributed to ʿAlī adds “vicissitudes of time” and further words; Qurṭubī says this is not recited Qurʾān and the received muṣḥaf text is correct.
QURTUBI:103:2/r9.anchor: وكان علي يقرؤها ( والعصر ونوائب الدهر ،   إن الإنسان لفي خسر

QURTUBI:103:2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r10.speaker: إبراهيم
QURTUBI:103:2/r10.claim: Ibrāhīm says aging and weakness bring decline except for believers whose youthful deeds continue to be credited, comparing it to 95:4–5; he transmits expanded wording that Qurṭubī rejects as Qurʾān.
QURTUBI:103:2/r10.anchor: وقال إبراهيم : إن الإنسان إذا عمر في الدنيا وهرم ،   لفي نقص وضعف تراجع

QURTUBI:103:2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:103:2/r11.claim: The sound text is the reading followed by the community and muṣḥafs; wording that opposes the ʿUthmānic codex is not Qurʾān to recite.
QURTUBI:103:2/r11.anchor: والصحيح ما عليه الأمة والمصاحف .   وقد مضى الرد في مقدمة الكتاب

QURTUBI:103:3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:103:3/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
QURTUBI:103:3/r3.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb asks the Prophet for the sūra’s meaning: the oath is by late day, the human in loss is Abū Jahl, faith is Abū Bakr, righteous deeds ʿUmar, truth ʿUthmān, and patience ʿAlī; Ibn ʿAbbās also preached this as a Companion report.
QURTUBI:103:3/r3.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب : قرأت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم { والعصر } ما تفسيرها يا نبي الله
